question_text: The angles of quadrilateral are in the ratio 3: 5: 9: 13. Find all the angles of the quadrilateral.

steps.description: Let the common ratio between the angles be x.
Set up the equation for the sum of angles: 3x + 5x + 9x + 13x = 360º.
Solve for x: x = 12º.
Calculate each angle using x.

final_answer: Therefore, the angles of the quadrilateral are 36º, 60º, 108º, and 156º.

question_image.description: Diagram showing parallelogram ABCD with points P and Q on diagonal BD.

parts.answer_text: In ∆APD and ∆CQB, ADP = CBQ (Alternate interior angles for BC || AD), AD = CB (Opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD), DP = BQ (Given). Therefore, ∆APD ∆CQB (Using SAS congruence rule).

State that AD = CB as opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD.
Use the given condition DP = BQ.
Apply the SAS congruence rule to conclude that ∆APD is congruent to ∆CQB.

parts.answer_text: Since ∆APD ∆CQB, by CPCT, AP = CQ.
In ∆AQB and ∆CPD, ABQ = CDP (Alternate interior angles for AB || CD), AB = CD (Opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD), BQ = DP (Given). Therefore, ∆AQB ∆CPD (Using SAS congruence rule).

State that AB = CD as opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD.
Use the given condition BQ = DP.
Apply the SAS congruence rule to conclude that ∆AQB is congruent to ∆CPD.

parts.answer_text: Since ∆AQB ∆CPD, by CPCT, AQ = CP.

question_text: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which P, Q, R and S are mid-points of the sides AB, BC, CD and DA. AC is a diagonal. Show that: (i) SR || AC and SR = AC (ii) PQ = SR (iii) PQRS is a parallelogram.

parts.part_text: Show that SR || AC and SR = AC.
parts.answer_text: In triangle ADC, S and R are the mid-points of sides AD and CD respectively. Therefore, SR || AC and SR = AC.

steps.description: Identify S and R as mid-points of sides AD and CD in triangle ADC.
Apply the mid-point theorem which states that the line segment joining the mid-points of two sides is parallel to the third side and half its length.

parts.final_answer: Thus, SR is parallel to AC and equal to AC.

parts.answer_text: In triangle ABC, P and Q are mid-points of sides AB and BC respectively. Therefore, by using the mid-point theorem, PQ || AC and PQ = AC. Since SR = AC, we have PQ = SR.

steps.description: Identify P and Q as mid-points of sides AB and BC in triangle ABC.
Apply the mid-point theorem to conclude that PQ is parallel to AC and equal to AC.
Since SR = AC, it follows that PQ = SR.

parts.answer_text: Since PQ || SR and PQ = SR, by definition, PQRS is a parallelogram.

question_text: In a parallelogram ABCD, E and F are the mid-points of sides AB and CD respectively. Show that the line segments AF and EC trisect the diagonal BD.

question_image.description: Figure showing parallelogram ABCD with midpoints E and F on sides AB and CD, respectively.

answer_text: ABCD is a parallelogram. AB || CD and hence, AE || FC. Again, AB = CD (Opposite sides of parallelogram ABCD). AE = FC (E and F are mid-points of side AB and CD). In quadrilateral AECF, one pair of opposite sides (AE and CF) is parallel and equal to each other. Therefore, AECF is a parallelogram. AF || EC (Opposite sides of a parallelogram). In ∆DQC, F is the mid-point of side DC and FP || CQ (as AF || EC). Therefore, by using converse of mid-point theorem, it can be said that P is the mid-point of DQ.

steps.description: Identify that ABCD is a parallelogram and establish parallel sides.
Show that AE is parallel to FC and equal in length.
Conclude that AECF is a parallelogram, thus AF is parallel to EC.
Use the converse of the mid-point theorem to show that P is the mid-point of DQ.

final_answer: Thus, AF and EC trisect the diagonal BD.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of properties of parallelograms and mid-point theorem.

question_text: Show that the line segments joining the mid-points of the opposite sides of a quadrilateral bisect each other.
answer_text: Let ABCD be a quadrilateral in which P, Q, R, and S are the mid-points of sides AB, BC, CD, and DA respectively. Join PQ, QR, RS, SP, and BD. In triangle ABD, S and P are the mid-points of AD and AB respectively. Therefore, by using the mid-point theorem, it can be said that SP || BD and SP = BD. Similarly in triangle BCD, QR || BD and QR = BD. From these equations, we obtain SP || QR and SP = QR. In quadrilateral SPQR, one pair of opposite sides is equal and parallel to each other. Therefore, SPQR is a parallelogram. We know that diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other. Hence, PR and QS bisect each other.

steps.description: Identify mid-points P, Q, R, and S of quadrilateral ABCD.
Apply the mid-point theorem in triangles ABD and BCD.
Conclude that SPQR is a parallelogram and its diagonals bisect each other.

final_answer: Therefore, the line segments joining the mid-points of the opposite sides of a quadrilateral bisect each other.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of mid-point theorem and properties of parallelograms.
